node_2.tagline: The open source Firebase alternative with relational PostgreSQL
node_2.purpose: Gives developers a dedicated PostgreSQL database with real-time subscriptions, instant REST and GraphQL APIs, Auth, and Storage, without vendor lock-in.
node_2.howItWorks: Wraps PostgreSQL with PostgREST (for automatic REST API generation), Realtime engine (listening to Postgres replication stream via Elixir), GoTrue for Auth, and Kong API gateway.
architecture: PostgreSQL: Full relational engine with extensions (pgvector, PostGIS)
PostgREST: Auto-generated REST endpoints from Postgres schemas and tables
Row Level Security (RLS): Native Postgres security policies determining row access per JWT token
Realtime Server: Elixir cluster broadcasting database change events over WebSockets
Edge Functions: Deno-based serverless functions at the edge
node_2.freeTierInfo: Free Tier: 2 active projects, 500 MB database, 1 GB file storage, 50k monthly active users, 500k edge function invocations.

# Supabase Technical Analysis

**Purpose:** Gives developers a dedicated PostgreSQL database with real-time subscriptions, instant REST and GraphQL APIs, Auth, and Storage, without vendor lock-in.

## Architecture
PostgreSQL: Full relational engine with extensions (pgvector, PostGIS),PostgREST: Auto-generated REST endpoints from Postgres schemas and tables,Row Level Security (RLS): Native Postgres security policies determining row access per JWT token,Realtime Server: Elixir cluster broadcasting database change events over WebSockets,Edge Functions: Deno-based serverless functions at the edge

## Official Docs
https://supabase.com/docs

node_2.tagline: Google's comprehensive mobile and web app development platform
node_2.purpose: Provides backend infrastructure (NoSQL Firestore, Authentication, Cloud Storage, Cloud Functions, Hosting, Analytics) so developers can build apps quickly without managing physical servers.
node_2.howItWorks: Operates as a Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) built on top of Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Clients interact directly with Firestore and Auth using client-side SDKs with security rules handling authorization, while Cloud Functions execute event-driven serverless Node/Python logic.
architecture: Cloud Firestore: Scalable NoSQL document database with real-time listeners and offline sync
Firebase Auth: Managed identity supporting Email/Password, Google, GitHub, Apple OAuth, and Phone SMS
Cloud Storage: Object storage for photos, audio, videos with granular security rules
Cloud Functions: Serverless event-driven compute triggered by Firestore writes, Auth events, or HTTPS requests
Security Rules: Declarative authorization expressions evaluated per request
node_2.freeTierInfo: Spark Plan (Free): 1 GB Firestore storage, 50k reads/day, 20k writes/day, 10 GB hosting transfer/month, phone auth 10k/month.
